source: Per-company AR extraction (Screener.in PDFs + IR sites) — Claude.ai routine, daily batch of 20

china_plus_one.evidence: Sell-side analysts (Jefferies, Mirae Asset Sharekhan) attribute custom-synthesis growth partly to a China+1/BIOSECURE-linked tailwind and expect ~16% CAGR through FY28 aided by this shift. However, on the FY25 earnings call, when asked directly whether custom synthesis order growth reflected business moving away from China, Divi's management was non-committal: it said it was seeing more RFPs and customer interest but found it difficult to say whether molecules were brought from China or were old molecules from existing portfolios. So the China+1 narrative is market/analyst-driven rather than a claim the company itself makes explicitly.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Divi's is reported as effectively debt-free (total debt ~Rs 89 crore vs equity ~Rs 15,410 crore, debt-to-equity ~0.6%), implying minimal exposure to floating-rate liabilities, but no explicit floating-vs-fixed debt split was found.

crude_exposure.evidence: Key inputs include methanol, imported solvents and other petrochemical-derived intermediates/solvents sourced partly from the Middle East, indirectly linked to crude oil price movements. Analyst commentary notes operating margins compressed to ~32% from a historical ~37-38%, partly due to elevated raw-material and freight costs, mitigated via long-term supply contracts and backward integration (e.g., Kakinada plant). No specific disclosed percentage was found.

inr_exposure.evidence: Exports were ~88% of FY25 revenue, but the largest single market is Europe (~56% of total revenue) rather than North America (~16%), implying meaningful EUR exposure alongside USD. CARE Ratings has flagged forex fluctuation risk as a rating constraint. Specific hedging policy text could not be retrieved.

pli_scheme.evidence: No source found confirming Divi's Laboratories as an approved beneficiary under India's PLI scheme for bulk drugs/APIs; Divi's was not identified among named beneficiaries in sources reviewed. Should be treated as 'not confirmed' rather than a definitive negative.

china_plus_one.evidence: Lupin frames its API/CDMO arm (Lupin Manufacturing Solutions / 'API Plus') as positioned to capture global supply-chain diversification: 'As the world seeks secure and diversified API sources, Lupin's API Plus business, built on decades of process chemistry and fermentation expertise, offers global customers credible, cost-effective, and high-quality solutions... With global pharma companies diversifying away from China, India's CDMO market is projected to grow from USD 3.5 Bn to USD 25 Bn over the next decade.' Forward-looking market-opportunity framing rather than an explicit claim that current-year revenue growth was already driven by China+1 shifts, so scored moderate rather than strong.

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Lupin operates in 100+ markets and is exposed to USD-INR, EUR-INR and ZAR-INR fluctuations; deploys natural hedges plus forex derivatives, with treasury operations applying a 'layered hedging strategy' (per Integrated Report 2024-25 risk-management content).
inr_exposure.evidence: US alone was ~36-38% of FY25 global sales and the company sells across 100+ export markets, implying majority of consolidated revenue is USD/hard-currency-linked, but no single disclosed 'USD revenue %' figure was found in accessible sources.

pli_scheme.evidence: Lupin, via its Aurangabad and Ankleshwar plants, is listed as a Category 1 (integrated formulator with complex-generics pipeline) applicant under India's Pharmaceuticals PLI scheme (Rs 15,000 crore outlay; Category 1 annual incentive capped at Rs 100 crore per applicant). No company-specific PLI revenue/incentive amount for Lupin was found.

china_plus_one.evidence: ABB India news center ('Symbiosis of Make in India and exports for sustainable growth'): India hosts '10 state-of-the-art global feeder factories' making products 'not only to fulfill domestic requirements but also ABB's global requirements'; the Vadodara Distribution Automation factory is described as 'the sole manufacturer' of Relion 605-series protection relays 'in over 60 countries where ABB operates worldwide,' having shipped 100,000+ units. Separately, ABB announced a ~$75M investment to expand Indian manufacturing/R&D for 'critical segments' and deepen its localization strategy. However, per the Q4 CY2024 earnings call, exports remain only ~10% of the business mix and management said exports are 'not a primary focus' (decided by global divisions based on market needs) — no explicit 'China+1' terminology or revenue-growth attribution to it was found in available sources.

govt_capex.evidence: Q4 CY2024 earnings call: 'Direct exposure to government customers is minimal, with indirect exposure through EPCs at about 35% to 40%.' Management also stated ABB India 'remains a beneficiary of the government's capex investments in mega infrastructure and renewable projects,' plus industrial capex in metals & mining, energy/chemicals, and buildings/data centers. Order backlog stood at INR 9,380-9,400 crore as of Dec 31, 2024 (+12% YoY), split roughly 40-50% long-gestation projects vs 50-60% short-cycle orders.

crude_exposure.evidence: No ABB-India-specific raw material cost % was located. ABB Group's (global parent) SEC/20-F disclosures note the company 'purchases large amounts of commodity-based raw materials, including steel, copper, aluminum and oil,' with prices subject to fluctuation — but no India-entity-specific breakdown was found in accessible sources.

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: ABB Group global policy: hedge material currency exposures via offsetting transactions with third-party financial institutions (no assurance hedges fully offset FX impact); no ABB-India-specific USD revenue % or hedging disclosure was located.
inr_exposure.evidence: Same as hedging_policy field; sourced from ABB Group-level disclosures, not an India-entity-specific figure.

pli_scheme.evidence: No evidence found of ABB India participating in any Production Linked Incentive scheme. India's PLI program covers 14 sectors (electronics/IT hardware, solar PV modules, auto & auto components, telecom, specialty steel, textiles, white goods, etc.); heavy electrical equipment/switchgear/transformers/relays — ABB India's core product lines — are not among currently PLI-covered sectors, and no company disclosure claiming PLI benefits was found.

china_plus_one.evidence: MD&A (Industry Overview): 'This export growth can be attributed to the positive global sentiment towards sourcing from India, fuelled by the China Plus One diversification strategy adopted by many companies... Traditional components such as castings, forgings, and injection moulded parts are expected to find export-oriented production opportunities in India as they become less viable in Western markets.' This is framed as an industry/ACMA-level trend, not attributed specifically to Gabriel India's own order or revenue growth — the Company's own export revenue is only ~2.7-3% of total turnover (BRSR states exports were 3.08% of total turnover in FY2023-24).

rural.evidence: AR does not disclose a distinct 'rural revenue' metric, but Company-specific MD&A states: 'the Company's 2W and 3W segment recorded a revenue of Rs 2,022.4 Cr. in FY2023-24... contributing approximately 61% to the Company's total revenue' (top customers TVS Motors, Suzuki Motorcycle, Honda Motorcycle & Scooter India) — two/three-wheelers carry meaningful rural/semi-urban demand sensitivity, making this the closest disclosed proxy. Separately, BRSR workforce-location data shows 66.39% of wage cost is in 'Rural' locations (FY23-24 vs 66.01% FY22-23), though this is an employee-cost metric, not a revenue metric.

govt_capex.evidence: Company has a Commercial Vehicles and Railways SBU and R&D references 'Design of Solar tracker dampers for Solar energy farms' and 'locomotive railway dampers,' implying some government/infrastructure-capex-linked exposure, but no revenue percentage tied to government capex or railways is disclosed in MD&A or segment notes.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Company (standalone) reports Debt-Equity Ratio of 0.01x (FY2023-24), effectively near debt-free; no interest rate risk sensitivity section appears in Note 36 Financial Risk Management (only commodity price risk and foreign currency risk are covered). On a consolidated basis, the only borrowing disclosed is a subsidiary's (Inalfa Gabriel Sunroof Systems) unsecured short-term working capital demand loan of Rs 251.67 million which carries variable interest linked to 3 months MCLR p.a and 6 months MCLR — against this the Group holds net cash of Rs 865.70 million, i.e., the Group is net-cash overall, so floating-rate exposure is immaterial.

crude_exposure.evidence: Note 36(C) Market risk - Commodity price sensitivity: 'The Company has significant usage of commodities like Steel, Oil, Aluminum exposing it to price risk arising out of market fluctuations... As the Company has a back to back pass through arrangements for volatility in raw material prices there is limited impact on the profit and loss and equity of the Company.' No raw-material-mix percentage (e.g. % oil/rubber-derived vs steel) is disclosed.

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Company uses foreign exchange forward contracts as cash-flow hedges; disclosed hedge ratios: 25% of expected 12-month exposure, 50% of 9-month, 75% of 6-month, 100% of 3-month expected exposure. Primary exposure currencies: USD, CNH (RMB), EUR, JPY.
inr_exposure.evidence: Note 36(D) Market risk - Foreign currency risk: 'The Company enters into international transactions and is exposed to resultant foreign exchange risk, primarily with respect to the USD, CNH (RMB), EUR and JPY... The objective of the hedges is to minimise the volatility of the INR cash flows of highly probable forecast transactions.' Net FX exposure amounts are disclosed in absolute INR millions (e.g., hedged USD net exposure Rs 32.35 million), not as a % of revenue.

pli_scheme.evidence: PLI is referenced only as a macro/industry-level government initiative in the Industry Overview section ('the government has rolled out targeted initiatives... including an over seven-fold increase in the allocation for the Production Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme for automobiles and auto components to Rs 3,500 Cr. in FY2024-25' and 'the government's PLI scheme with an outlay of USD 3.5 billion is bolstering domestic manufacturing'). No statement anywhere in the AR indicates Gabriel India itself is an approved/participating PLI beneficiary or discloses PLI-linked revenue.

rural.evidence: Not disclosed; rural revenue split not applicable/reported for a pharmaceutical formulations & API business

govt_capex.evidence: Not disclosed; not applicable to Sun Pharma's business model

pli_scheme.evidence: Sun Pharma was selected under the Government of India's Production Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme for promotion of domestic manufacturing of critical Key Starting Materials (KSMs)/Drug Intermediates and APIs, alongside peers including Aurobindo Pharma, Dr Reddy's, Lupin, Cipla, and Cadila Healthcare; also reported among 55 pharma companies selected under the broader Rs 15,000 crore PLI scheme for the pharmaceutical sector (per Swarajya Mag / PIB press releases, not verified directly against the AR text).

rural.evidence: Alkem derives ~80-85% of revenue from the acute therapeutic segment (anti-infectives, GI, pain management, vitamins/minerals/nutrients), which skews toward rural/Tier 2-3-4 town demand; trade generics (sold via retailers/distributors rather than physician promotion, ~Rs 2,400 crore) grew as a response to tier 2/3 town access gaps during COVID. No explicit numeric 'rural revenue %' was disclosed in sources accessible this session.

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Per CFO commentary referenced in earnings-call coverage, Alkem hedges roughly 80% of its forex exposure; US-linked generics revenue provides a partial natural hedge but introduces translation effects during FX volatility.
inr_exposure.evidence: US business contributed 19.4% of total FY25 sales (down from higher share in FY24 amid 10.4% US de-growth); total international sales were 29.8% of FY25 revenue (Rs 3,821 crore), down from 32.2% in FY24, with non-US markets (Australia, Europe, Latin America) growing ~28.2% YoY.

pli_scheme.evidence: No Alkem-specific mention of PLI (Production Linked Incentive) scheme participation was found in sources accessible this session; general PLI bulk-drug/KSM scheme details were found but did not name Alkem as an approved beneficiary.

china_plus_one.evidence: JB Pharma's CDMO business is described as ranking among the top 5 global CDMO players in lozenges, with a robust order book and recent global development project wins. Management's strategy emphasizes strengthening international diversification, scaling India + CDMO to 75-80% of total revenue medium-term, deepening the CDMO client base, and expanding into newer regulated geographies. No source explicitly frames this as China+1, so treated as general export/CDMO growth momentum.

inr_exposure.evidence: FY25 revenue split reported as ~58% domestic / ~42% international (segmental revenue cited as Domestic Rs2,269 Cr, International formulations Rs1,128 Cr, CDMO Rs446 Cr, API Rs76 Cr). International exposure spans multiple currencies (RUB via Russia subsidiary, ZAR via South Africa subsidiary, US sales via Rising Pharma on cost-plus model, exports from Panoli facility), so a single USD-revenue percentage could not be confirmed.

pli_scheme.evidence: No source found confirms JB Chemicals & Pharmaceuticals as a named beneficiary/selected applicant under India's PLI scheme for bulk drugs/APIs or KSMs.

china_plus_one.evidence: No China+1 / supply-chain diversification narrative found. Torrent Pharma's disclosed model is branded-generics/chronic-therapy focused (India + Brazil branded markets ~73% of revenue combined), not an API/CDMO export story tied to China+1 dynamics, despite having API capacity at its Indrad (Gujarat) plant.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Torrent Pharma financed its ~Rs 25,700 crore JB Chemicals acquisition largely via non-convertible debentures/bonds (tranches priced ~7.15%-7.5%, AA+ rated), i.e. fixed-rate instruments per deal reporting, but no explicit disclosed floating-rate-liability percentage of total debt was found.

inr_exposure.evidence: FY25 revenue by geography reported as approximately India 55%, Brazil 10%, US 10%, Germany 10%, Other markets 15%, implying multi-currency exposure (USD, BRL, EUR) rather than a single USD-revenue figure.

pli_scheme.evidence: Torrent Pharmaceuticals is listed as one of the approved applicants under India's PLI Scheme for Pharmaceuticals (Department of Pharmaceuticals), Group A / Category 1, alongside Sun Pharma, Dr. Reddy's, Cipla, Lupin, etc. No revenue percentage tied to PLI incentives was disclosed.

china_plus_one.evidence: No China+1 / supply-chain diversification narrative found. Company's international exposure relates to overseas EPC project execution (Sri Lanka, Bangladesh, and a ~Rs 10,000 Cr Middle East pipeline) rather than manufacturing supply-chain diversification away from China.

govt_capex.evidence: Company (formerly ITD Cementation India Ltd, renamed Cemindia Projects Ltd after Adani-linked Renew Exim DMCC acquired control in May 2025) executes large-scale public/quasi-public infrastructure projects (metro/MRTS, ports, airports, highways, dams & tunnels) predominantly for government and PSU clients. Per ICRA rating rationale, unexecuted order book as of March 31, 2025 (~Rs 18,300 Cr) was ~95% domestic (13 states, 1 UT) and ~5% international. Exact % of revenue specifically from government-funded projects was not disclosed.

crude_exposure.evidence: Raw material exposure is primarily to steel, cement and bitumen prices for construction projects; no explicit crude-oil-linked raw material percentage disclosed.

inr_exposure.evidence: International order book (Sri Lanka, Bangladesh, Middle East pipeline) represented ~5% of total unexecuted order book as of March 2025; revenue-based forex exposure and hedging policy not disclosed.

pli_scheme.evidence: PLI (Production Linked Incentive) schemes are not applicable to the civil/EPC construction sector; no mention found.

china_plus_one.evidence: Sona Comstar signed a $20M JV (60% stake, $12M cash investment) with China's Jinnaite Machinery Co. to manufacture driveline systems locally in China. Coverage frames this as strengthening Sona's 'China+1 strategy in reverse' — not moving away from China but partnering within it — aiming for a geographically diversified, vertically integrated presence across North America, Europe, and Asia (the three key EV markets). Company also noted ~12-15% of raw materials are imported, mainly from China, mitigated by hedging policy.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Company carries very low debt levels (long-term debt ~Rs 80 million in FY25, down from ~Rs 292 million in FY24); specific floating- vs fixed-rate borrowing split not disclosed.

crude_exposure.evidence: Primary raw material exposure is to steel/metal alloys (forged components), not crude oil derivatives; ~12-15% of raw material requirements are imported, mainly from China.

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Company maintains an active forex hedging policy to mitigate risk from its high international revenue base (59% of FY25 revenue from exports, split ~30% North America and ~24% Europe) and imported raw materials.
inr_exposure.evidence: 'This forex exposure is mitigated to a certain extent by the company's effective hedging policy' (India Ratings press release); ~74% of revenue was international in FY22, moderating to ~59% (41% domestic) by FY25.

pli_scheme.evidence: Sona Comstar became the first automotive component manufacturer in India to receive PLI (Auto PLI scheme) certification, for its EV traction motor (hub wheel drive motor for electric two-wheelers), out of seven applications filed across product categories. Specific revenue % attributable to PLI-linked products not disclosed.

china_plus_one.evidence: OFSS is a banking/financial-services software provider; its international revenue reflects global software licensing and services demand, not manufacturing supply-chain diversification from China. No China+1 narrative found.

crude_exposure.evidence: Not applicable — software/IT services company with no material raw material or crude-linked input costs.

inr_exposure.evidence: Exports have historically contributed ~88-90% of OFSS's total turnover (company operates in 47 countries with clients including multinational, regional and central banks); analyst commentary notes Indian rupee appreciation against the USD could impact OFSS earnings. Note: the 88.4% export figure was sourced from a report referencing FY26 turnover (Rs 57,167 million) rather than confirmed directly for FY2024-25 (Rs 6,847 Cr revenue); treated as a reasonable proxy given the ratio's historical stability, but exact FY24-25 figure and formal hedging policy were not confirmed from the primary annual report.

pli_scheme.evidence: Not applicable — PLI schemes target manufacturing sectors; OFSS is a software/IT services company.

china_plus_one.evidence: No explicit company-level China+1 / API supply-chain diversification narrative was found in Mankind-specific sources. Company completed a multi-year global supply chain and procurement transformation (with Accenture) covering >25 international markets, but this was framed around digital/AI-enabled planning rather than explicit China+1 positioning.

rural.evidence: Per Mankind Pharma's FY2023-24 Annual Report (most recent disclosure found), Tier 6 Cities and Rural markets accounted for 47% of revenue distribution, with the remaining 53% from other segments — reflecting the company's strategic focus on rural/underserved market reach via its large field force (17,700+ members covering 5 lakh+ doctors). FY2024-25-specific figure not confirmed in sources reviewed.

govt_capex.evidence: Not directly applicable — revenue driven by branded generics/consumer healthcare distribution rather than government capex.

crude_exposure.evidence: Raw material inputs are APIs/KSMs (some petrochemical-derived intermediates); company has ~500 MT installed API capacity, but no explicit crude-oil-linked cost percentage disclosed.

inr_exposure.evidence: FY25 revenue was Rs 12,207.44 Cr (up 18.97% YoY), of which domestic revenue was Rs 10,675 Cr (up 13.0% YoY, ~87.5% of total), implying exports of ~Rs 1,532 Cr (~12.5%). Export growth was notably strong intra-year (57% YoY export growth reported in Q2 FY25). Formal hedging policy not disclosed.

pli_scheme.evidence: Mankind Pharma does not appear among the major named beneficiaries of the pharma/bulk-drug PLI schemes (Dr Reddy's, Cipla, Glenmark, Biocon, Wockhardt cited as key beneficiaries); no mention of Mankind PLI participation found.

china_plus_one.evidence: No China+1 / supply-chain-relocation narrative found. Eicher/Royal Enfield is a domestic-manufacturing, India-centric 2-wheeler brand with a growing but still small export volume (~10% of motorcycle units in FY25) rather than a beneficiary of manufacturers relocating away from China.

rural.evidence: Third-party commentary indicates rural growth outpaced urban for Royal Enfield in FY25, with improved rural demand attributed to GST cuts on sub-350cc motorcycles/scooters and better financing availability. No specific rural revenue/volume percentage was disclosed in accessible sources.

govt_capex.evidence: VECV (Volvo Eicher Commercial Vehicles JV) posted its best-ever annual sales in FY25 (82,450 units, +15.7% YoY), with commentary attributing commercial-vehicle demand growth to sustained infrastructure capex; VECV's LMD bus strength tied partly to government/state bus contracts (~35% bus segment share). No AR-disclosed percentage of revenue tied specifically to government capex was found.

crude_exposure.evidence: Third-party summaries describe a ~3-3.5% commodity cost inflation headwind in FY25 from steel, rubber and base metals (not crude oil directly). No AR-disclosed raw material cost as % of revenue/COGS was accessible.

inr_exposure.evidence: Exports were ~10% of Royal Enfield motorcycle volumes in FY25 (100,136 of 1,002,893 units), up 29.7% YoY. No specific USD-denominated revenue percentage or forex hedging policy details were found.

pli_scheme.evidence: Eicher Motors is listed among approved applicants under India's PLI Scheme for Automobile and Auto Component Industry, 'Champion OEM Incentive Scheme,' General Vehicle category, per Ministry of Heavy Industries/pliauto.in. Appears linked to commercial-vehicle (VECV) investment rather than Royal Enfield two-wheelers. No incentive amount or revenue percentage disclosed.

china_plus_one.evidence: Secondary summary (not primary AR) notes Indian steelmakers incl. Shyam Metalics are pivoting to specialised/high-margin products (automotive, speciality alloys, CRGO, stainless) partly to reduce exposure to commoditized-steel dumping from China. Management quote (via secondary source, not verified against primary transcript): 'We do not see any surge in import bookings as of now' regarding Chinese import risk. This reads as risk-monitoring commentary rather than an explicit strategic China+1 growth narrative.

govt_capex.evidence: No company-specific % disclosed in sources accessed. Third-party commentary links long-products demand (TMT bars, wire rods, structural steel) to government infra spend, railway modernization, and PMAY housing scheme, but this is sector-level framing, not a Shyam Metalics-specific quantified revenue exposure.

rate_sensitive.evidence: No floating-rate debt % found. Secondary financial summaries note conservative leverage (debt/equity ~0.18, interest coverage ~11.8x) and finance costs up ~43% YoY with working-capital debt rising to ~Rs 1,100 crore to fund value-added segment expansion, but no note-level floating vs fixed rate split was accessible.

crude_exposure.evidence: Not crude-oil-linked — Shyam Metalics' primary inputs are iron ore, coking/thermal coal, and manganese/chrome ore, not crude oil. Iron ore and coal sourced substantially from captive mines and third parties in Odisha/eastern India, plants sited within ~250km of the mineral belt, ~300MW captive power capacity used to reduce input cost volatility. No AR-sourced cost-sensitivity % was accessible.

inr_exposure.evidence: Export share (~10-11% of revenue) implies a similar order of USD-linked revenue exposure per secondary financial commentary. No forex/forward-contract hedging note was directly accessible.

pli_scheme.evidence: Company confirmed (via press coverage of the Cold Rolling Mill project at Jamuria, West Bengal) as a beneficiary under the Government's PLI Scheme (PLI 2.0) for specialty steel/downstream products. Phase 1 (0.25 MTPA) commissioned earlier; Phase 2 (0.15 MTPA GI/Galvalume line, total capex ~Rs 603 crore) reached commercial production April 2026, bringing total CRM capacity to 0.40 MTPA. No revenue % attributable to PLI-linked output was disclosed.

china_plus_one.evidence: Third-party analyst/industry commentary indicates Glenmark's API business is expected to benefit as global customers diversify sourcing away from China ('China+1'); Glenmark operates 5 API manufacturing plants (of 14 total facilities across India, US, Argentina, Czech Republic). Could not directly access AR MD&A/notes text to confirm company's own framing or quantify benefit, so marked moderate rather than strong.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Glenmark has been deleveraging (gross borrowings reported around Rs 2,473 Cr as of Mar 2025, down further in subsequent quarters); specific fixed-vs-floating rate debt composition for FY25 not found in accessible sources.

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Global CFO has stated the company relies substantially on natural hedging for currency exposure (per third-party interview reference), rather than heavy use of derivative hedges. Could not verify exact policy language from the AR's financial risk management note directly.
inr_exposure.evidence: Export revenue (~66% of consolidated, spanning North America, Europe, and RoW/API markets) implies material USD and other foreign-currency exposure, but an explicit disclosed USD revenue % figure was not found.

pli_scheme.evidence: Glenmark Pharma was one of 9 domestic companies (out of 11 applicants) approved in Group A under the Government of India's PLI Scheme for Promotion of Domestic Manufacturing of Critical KSMs/Drug Intermediates (DIs)/APIs, administered by the Department of Pharmaceuticals. Specific PLI incentive income/revenue contribution for FY25 not found.

china_plus_one.evidence: No explicit China+1 or supply-chain-diversification-away-from-China commentary was located. Usha Martin has a global manufacturing/export footprint (plants in Ranchi, Hoshiarpur, Dubai, Bangkok, UK; international revenue ~55% of FY25 total, serving oil & gas, mining, elevator, port and crane end-markets), circumstantially consistent with a China+1-style demand shift, but this cannot be confirmed as a stated narrative without the AR.

rural.evidence: Usha Martin is an industrial/infrastructure-facing specialty steel wire and wire rope manufacturer (mining, oil & gas, elevators, ports, cranes, construction) with no direct rural consumer revenue segment disclosed; rural exposure is not applicable/not disclosed.

govt_capex.evidence: Secondary-source summaries of FY25 results state demand was driven by sectors such as oil and gas, mining, and infrastructure, with products supplied across oil & gas, elevators, ports, cranes, and mining. No specific % of revenue tied to government capex/infrastructure was disclosed.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Company reported consolidated net debt of only ~Rs 63 crore at FY25-end, implying low overall leverage and limited interest-rate sensitivity. No specific floating-vs-fixed borrowing mix was accessible.

crude_exposure.evidence: Not a crude-oil cost exposure business. Usha Martin is vertically integrated with captive iron ore and coal mines feeding its own steel/wire-rod production. Primary cost driver is steel/wire-rod/iron-ore, not crude oil. Demand-side note: supplies wire ropes/OCTG to oil & gas drilling sector, so crude-price-driven E&P capex could indirectly affect demand, but this is not a raw-material cost linkage.

inr_exposure.evidence: International revenue was ~55% of FY25 consolidated revenue, with manufacturing/sales presence in the US, UK, Dubai, Bangkok and Singapore implying multi-currency (USD, GBP, EUR, AED, THB) exposure, not solely USD. No specific USD-denominated revenue % or hedging policy detail was found.

pli_scheme.evidence: No confirmation found that Usha Martin is an approved/selected beneficiary under the Government of India's PLI Scheme for Specialty Steel. One analyst commentary snippet vaguely stated the company 'benefits from the PLI scheme continuity' as a sector tailwind, but this reads as broker commentary rather than a confirmed company disclosure.

rural.evidence: Rural/rural-to-urban migration references in AR relate only to CSR initiatives (e.g. women's entrepreneurship programme curbing rural-to-urban migration) and macro RBI commentary on rural consumption, not a disclosed hotel-revenue segment.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements, Note 37 Financial Risk Management (Interest rate risk): 'The Group adopts a policy to hedge the interest rate movement...partly by entering into fixed rate instruments and partly by borrowing at a floating rate...The total borrowing at variable rate was Rs.176.74 crores as at March 31, 2025 (March 31, 2024 - Rs.209.63 crores).' Total Group borrowings were Rs.224.70 crores as at March 31, 2025, implying ~78.7% of gross debt is floating-rate. Note: absolute debt quantum is very small — the Group is net-debt-cash-positive (net cash of Rs.2,848.52 crores as at March 31, 2025), so floating-rate exposure is not a material earnings risk currently. Standalone (parent-only) entity reported no borrowings as at March 31, 2025 and March 31, 2024.

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Group uses forward exchange contracts, interest rate swaps, currency swaps and options to hedge foreign currency and interest rate exposure, but had no such instruments outstanding at March 31, 2025 balance sheet date. Equity investments in international subsidiaries are long-term/strategic and deliberately not hedged.
inr_exposure.evidence: Note 37 Financial Risk Management (Foreign Currency risk): 'The predominant currency of the Group's revenue and operating cash flows is Indian Rupees.' Unhedged foreign currency exposure (payable) was USD 0.62 million as at March 31, 2025; a 3% INR/USD move affects PBT by only ~0.01%, indicating minimal transactional FX exposure at the standalone/parent level despite ~17.5% of consolidated revenue being overseas (revenue is largely earned and retained locally overseas rather than remitted/translated).

pli_scheme.evidence: PLI scheme is mentioned only in the AR's macroeconomic overview (RBI/manufacturing sector commentary) as a general economy driver, not as a scheme IHCL itself participates in or benefits from.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Could not access the primary Annual Report (Notes to Financial Statements / Financial Risk Management / borrowings note) or the company's IR site directly. Secondary sources (ICICIdirect/Gurufocus earnings summaries) indicate cost of debt fell from ~9.2% to ~8.5% in Q4 FY25, gross debt ~INR4,400 crore, net debt/EBITDA ~1.2x — consistent with meaningful project/construction debt typical for a mall developer, but no quantified floating-rate percentage was found.

inr_exposure.evidence: Secondary sources describe Phoenix Mills as operating 12+ retail-led mixed-use properties across 8 major Indian cities with no disclosed overseas/export operations; business appears fully domestic, but no explicit AR-quantified domestic/export revenue split was found.

rural.evidence: No explicit company-level revenue % for rural/tier-2-3-4 towns was found. Qualitative disclosures indicate strategic emphasis on non-metro expansion: FY25 network reported at 280+ clinical laboratories and 5,700-7,700+ patient service centres (PSCs) spanning tier 2/3/4 towns; FY25/FY26 capex plans (15-20 new labs, ~INR 60-70 crore) focused on building hub labs in northern and eastern tier 2/3/4 locations, plus franchisee-led expansion into tier-3/4 markets. Southern India markets reported to contribute only ~6% of consolidated revenue (indicating continued North-India/Delhi-NCR revenue concentration). Industry-level context (not company-specific): tier-3/4 towns already represent ~40% of India's overall diagnostics market revenue, growing ~25% annually.

govt_capex.evidence: Secondary commentary notes that Indian government schemes such as Ayushman Bharat Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (AB-PMJAY) and the PM Ayushman Bharat Health Infrastructure Mission (ABHIM) are cited as industry-wide growth drivers expanding diagnostics access in Tier-2/3 regions. No company-specific revenue attribution or % tied to government schemes was found.

inr_exposure.evidence: Low-reliability, unverified third-party claims suggest reagents/diagnostic instruments are partly imported (e.g. Thermo Fisher, Merck) creating some FX/cost sensitivity, with one unsourced claim that raw materials/reagents were ~30% of FY23 operating expenditure. rural.evidence: Company/media coverage indicates strategic focus on Tier-2/Tier-3 town expansion for Tanishq (network targeted to grow from ~800 to ~1,400 stores by FY30, with ~600 new stores planned over four years, many via franchisees in smaller towns), but no specific % of revenue or store count attributable to rural/smaller towns was found disclosed in MD&A.

crude_exposure.evidence: Not applicable — Titan's core raw materials are gold, diamonds and silver (jewellery segment) plus watch/eyewear components, not crude oil or petroleum derivatives. No crude oil exposure identified.

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Titan is widely reported (broker/media commentary) to follow a near-100% gold price hedging policy, sourcing gold via gold metal loans from banks, customer gold-exchange at stores (~40-50% of gold procured this way, acting as a natural hedge), and futures/forward contracts on spot-bought gold. Company has also sought RBI approval to use international currency forward contracts for gold-on-lease-related exposure due to limited domestic hedge liquidity.
inr_exposure.evidence: Titan operates an international jewellery footprint of ~23 stores (21 Tanishq + 2 Mia stores) across UAE, USA, Singapore and Qatar, plus 1 CaratLane store in the US, implying some USD-denominated revenue, but no USD revenue % of total was disclosed. Motilal Oswal and other broker notes describe Titan's gold hedging as 'among the highest in the industry.'

pli_scheme.evidence: No evidence found of Titan participating in any Production Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme. India's PLI schemes do not currently cover the gems & jewellery / watches sector.
